headline: Medium risk: kotaemon can ingest sensitive documents while rasa can relay outputs to chat channels, creating leakage and prompt-injection pathways; no direct shared-workspace evidence is provided.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests HTML, MHTML, PDFs, DOCX, and chat transcripts, so attacker-controlled content can enter its outputs; rasa then exposes conversation flows through messaging channels. No shared filesystem is documented, but the pair still has a plausible content-to-chat bridge, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF kotaemon outputs untrusted document text into a prompt that rasa later consumes, injection is possible.
IF rasa forwards model text into Slack, Telegram, or similar channels, malicious instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Add a fixed instruction delimiter around all kotaemon outputs.
Strip markup and code blocks before passing text from kotaemon to rasa.
Require human review for any rasa message derived from document content.
Use a denylist for prompt-like phrases in upstream document excerpts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags end-to-end.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and broad document types, while rasa connects to external messaging APIs. Even without a shared workspace, sensitive content from kotaemon can be surfaced through rasa channels, so the pair can leak documents or secrets in default support workflows.
conditions: IF kotaemon processes documents containing secrets or customer data, those contents can reach downstream chat outputs.
IF rasa is connected to Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar, those outputs may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff from kotaemon.
Disable forwarding of raw document excerpts into rasa responses.
Restrict rasa channels to non-sensitive test data.
Turn on message-level logging review for outbound support replies.
requires-engineering: implement data-class based routing and redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and broad network egress, while rasa does not support multiple instances and uses allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, so a direct conflict is not established; uncertainty keeps this at low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external bot channel or API token, write contention can occur.
IF an operator shares one mutable backend without locking, state conflicts become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate credentials to each agent.
Avoid sharing the same bot channel between both agents.
Serialize writes through one orchestrator.
Check for duplicate webhook registrations.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon can generate answers from documents and citations, and rasa is a dialogue system that can turn upstream text into user-facing replies. The profiles do not prove verification steps between them, so A's output may become B's authoritative response path in default support flows.
conditions: IF rasa consumes kotaemon-generated text without a verification layer, errors can cascade to users.
IF kotaemon hallucinates or misquotes sources, rasa may repeat the mistake in support replies.
mitigations: Require citation checks before rasa sends any answer.
Route uncertain kotaemon outputs to human review.
Limit rasa to templated responses when upstream confidence is low.
Log source passages alongside generated answers.
requires-engineering: add automated fact verification between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and document-heavy support data, while rasa integrates with third-party messaging platforms. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, but the pair can move customer-support content across external services, creating a plausible compliance mismatch that is not ruled out.
conditions: IF regulated customer data is processed through Slack, Telegram, Twilio, or similar, residency and retention obligations may be implicated.
IF kotaemon stores sensitive documents in ./ktem_app_data and rasa relays them externally, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Classify data before routing it through either agent.
Block regulated data from external messaging channels.
Review retention settings on both systems.
Document which jurisdictions each channel uses.
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing and retention controls.
